ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Higuchi Ichiyō — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Two-week review on treatment: culture result, liver tests, vision, and release from precautions

text.paragraph: Ms. Higuchi returns two weeks into treatment. She has taken all fourteen doses on daily video calls with the public health center nurse. The evening fevers stopped about ten days in, the night sweats are lighter, and the cough is less frequent and dry. She had mild nausea after the morning doses in the first week, which went once she moved them to bedtime with a small snack. Her urine and tears are orange, as expected. She has no yellowing, dark urine, abdominal pain, rash, numbness, or change in vision or colors. The liquid culture from her first sputum specimen grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex after twelve days. She is eating three meals and two snacks a day with the supplement drinks. The public funding was approved. She has begun to write again for about an hour each morning. [S]

tr.td: Less tired; weight 39.2 kg, up 0.7 kg; temperature 37.1 °C, pulse 90

Cough for about seven weeks with evening fevers, night sweats, poor appetite and weight loss of about 4 kg (about 10 percent) in a woman of 23; chest X-ray with patchy right upper lobe opacities and no cavity; suspected pulmonary tuberculosis; airborne precautions and three sputum specimens for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification and culture
S — Synthetic presenting problem at intake, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit; its timing echoes her documented decline from early 1896 (D).
Pulmonary tuberculosis of the right upper lobe, sputum smear-negative, confirmed by Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (Mycobacterium tuberculosis detected, low; rifampin resistance not detected)
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented tuberculosis; all bacteriology and imaging are synthetic.
Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: BMI 17.6, about 10 percent weight loss in two months, and albumin 3.3 g/dL
S — Synthetic nutrition diagnosis at intake, anchored to her documented poverty.
Low and irregular income from writing, with a household to support; costs of care are a barrier
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty and household responsibilities.
